original_question: Characterize injective C0-semigroups via the backward uniqueness property, and apply the resulting criteria to non-autonomous Cauchy problems u'(t) = A(t)u(t) with sectorial A(t) by analyzing the corresponding evolution semigroup.
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 27 (Backward uniqueness property), with nearby contextual support from Section 1, Problem 8 (Non-autonomous abstract Cauchy problems).
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual target. It correctly identifies the relevant notion as the backward uniqueness property, correctly paraphrases this as a characterization problem for injective C0-semigroups, and correctly includes the intended application to non-autonomous Cauchy problems of the form u'(t)=A(t)u(t) with sectorial A(t) through the associated evolution semigroup.
missing_details: The paper poses this as an open problem to study, not as an already established theorem with known criteria; the wording should not presuppose that the characterization has already been obtained.
The ambient setting should be made explicit: a one-parameter strongly continuous semigroup (T(t))_{t>=0} of bounded linear operators on a Banach space X.
The meaning of the backward uniqueness property should be spelled out explicitly: T(t)x=0 for some t>0 implies x=0; equivalently, the semigroup is injective.
For the non-autonomous part, it should be stated that the family A(t) acts on the same Banach space and that each A(t) is assumed sectorial.
To be fully stand-alone, the non-autonomous Cauchy problem should include an initial condition such as u(t0)=x0.
The application should remain specifically tied to the corresponding evolution semigroup, rather than being broadened to a general well-posedness or regularity problem.
refined_question: On a Banach space X, can one characterize those C0-semigroups (T(t))_{t>=0} that have the backward uniqueness property—equivalently, such that T(t)x=0 for some t>0 implies x=0—and then apply such a characterization to the non-autonomous Cauchy problem u'(t)=A(t)u(t), u(t0)=x0, where each A(t) is sectorial, by studying the associated evolution semigroup?
equivalent_formulation: Study the backward uniqueness property, i.e. characterize injective C0-semigroups, and apply the result to non-autonomous Cauchy problems u'(t)=A(t)u(t) with sectorial A(t) by examining the corresponding evolution semigroup.
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 7, Problem 27 of the paper, which states almost exactly this two-part problem: first, study backward uniqueness by characterizing injective C0-semigroups; second, apply that analysis to non-autonomous Cauchy problems with sectorial A(t) via the corresponding evolution semigroup. The nearby Section 1, Problem 8 supplies the paper's standard non-autonomous-Cauchy-problem/evolution-semigroup context on Banach spaces, so it is appropriate to use that only to make the question self-contained, not to broaden it beyond Problem 27.
